narrative.overview: Chat Engine should disappear behind the conversation. Its interface uses recognizable messenger structure, calm surfaces, compact controls, and one restrained blue accent so users can sign in, find a person, or open the assistant without learning a dashboard. The system takes familiarity from modern messaging products without copying their brand assets.
keyCharacteristics: Restrained blue actions against paper-white or ink-dark surfaces.
Compact rounded controls, circular identity marks, and calm asymmetric bubbles.
Equivalent light and dark modes with obvious, persistent switching.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Blue communicates action, selection, or message ownership; it is not general decoration.

rules.name: The Theme Parity Rule
rules.body: Every surface and state must remain legible and structurally identical in light and dark modes.

rules.name: The Quiet Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Repeated conversation UI stays compact; display scale belongs only to onboarding or true empty states.

rules.name: The Flat Shell Rule
rules.body: Persistent navigation and thread regions use borders and tonal layering; shadows are reserved for content or controls that visually float.

dos: Do keep sign-in, account creation, theme switching, conversation selection, and sending immediately discoverable.
Do preserve the two-pane desktop and one-pane mobile messenger model.
Do use semantic icon labels, visible keyboard focus, sufficient contrast, and reduced-motion support.
Do keep the assistant inside the conversation list while isolating its runtime behavior.
donts: Don't hide primary actions in a gear menu or ambiguous overflow control.
Don't reintroduce dashboard tabs, decorative cards, or competing chrome around the active conversation.
Don't expose placeholder message actions such as no-op retry or client-only destructive hide.
Don't copy WhatsApp or Telegram branding, proprietary assets, or signature colors literally.
